facts.text: Indigenous Coahuiltecan peoples originally inhabited the area encompassing present-day El Socio, roaming the brushy plains and river valleys for centuries.
El Socio sits just north of the Rio Grande, which forms the international boundary with Mexico to the south.
Early twentieth-century homesteads in the vicinity of La Victoria served as the precursor to the community of El Socio.
El Socio experiences a humid subtropical climate with hot, humid summers and average high temperatures reaching ninety-eight degrees in July.
Spanish colonial expansion in the mid-eighteenth century brought land grants to the region to encourage settlement and ranching.
El Socio covers a total land area of about zero point zero one one square miles with no incorporated water bodies.
